name: Buggy Choke to Triangle Control
summary: The bottom Buggy holder exchanges the arm-and-leg loop for a leg triangle around the neck and one arm, preserving the bottom actor through a continuous control transition.
description: The bottom Buggy holder exchanges the arm-and-leg loop for a leg triangle around the neck and one arm, preserving the bottom actor through a continuous control transition.
overview:
The bottom Buggy holder exchanges the arm-and-leg loop for a leg triangle around the neck and one arm, preserving the bottom actor through a continuous control transition.

Begin as the bottom player holding the same-side arm-and-leg Buggy loop beneath side control. Unload the choke before changing the leg and arm connections.

Recover the legs in front through the available space while keeping the knee movement comfortable. Exchange the Buggy loop for a leg triangle containing the opponent's neck and one arm. Count the transition only once Triangle Control/Bottom is secured; the actor remains the bottom holder. If ordinary guard settles before the triangle exists, use a separate valid guard entry. Losing the loop can also leave Side Control/Bottom.

Practice cooperatively with controlled movement. Stop at any tap, verbal signal, or distress; release all joint or neck pressure before changing direction. Do not force a trapped knee, shoulder, or neck to preserve the route.

defender.name: Buggy Choke to Triangle Control Defender
defender.description: Recognize Buggy Choke to Triangle Control and interrupt its required connections before the final control is established.
defender.overview:
You oppose the performer of this action. Maintain head and shoulder alignment while the loop opens. Keep the arm connected to the torso before the leg triangle forms. Use inside frames during the leg exchange. Recognize open guard if it settles before a triangle enclosure forms. Confirm side control only after the holder loses both the loop and the incoming leg control.

Practice cooperatively with controlled movement. Stop at any tap, verbal signal, or distress; release all joint or neck pressure before changing direction. Do not force a trapped knee, shoulder, or neck to preserve the route.

flashcards.question: Against Buggy Choke to Triangle Control, when must you stop moving?

flashcards.question: Against Buggy Choke to Triangle Control, does interrupting one grip guarantee a new position?
